title: Which drink mix is stronger
observableEvidence: Uses ratio tables to compare two ratios by scaling each to a common quantity.
prompt: Mix A uses 3 scoops of drink powder for every 5 cups of water. Mix B uses 5 scoops for every 8 cups of water. Use ratio tables to find how many scoops each mix needs for 40 cups of water. Then decide which mix tastes stronger (more powder for the same water).
solutionRepresentation: Mix A: 5 cups × 8 = 40 cups, so 3 × 8 = 24 scoops. Mix B: 8 cups × 5 = 40 cups, so 5 × 5 = 25 scoops. With the same 40 cups of water, Mix B uses more powder, so Mix B is stronger. Comparing differences (Mix A has 2 more cups than scoops, Mix B has 3) does not compare the ratios.
solutionMethod: Scale each ratio by multiplication to the common water amount, then compare the scoops at that common amount.

deterministicValidator.canonicalAnswer: Scoops in Mix A for 40 cups: 24 scoops; Scoops in Mix B for 40 cups: 25 scoops; Stronger mix: Mix B
acceptedAnswers: Scoops in Mix A for 40 cups: 24 scoops; Scoops in Mix B for 40 cups: 25 scoops; Stronger mix: Mix B
